supplied: 0x18defa0 and 0x18df0c0 vector reserve (tags 0x22/0x24; the common body is reconstructed as reserve_pose_pointer_vector but not run here)
method: Original merges run natively in Unicorn over the memory image; supplied callees are intercepted at entry and executed by one shared authored model (bump reserve, byte copy, reverse sort, logging). The Python modules run the same model over a PoseFlatMemory copy of the 0xb0000-byte fixture. The comparator runs natively and is compared to its signed 32-bit result.
comparisons: ordered service calls with every argument
provider vector descriptor snapshots at reserve, sort and finish, and provider count/pointer at every attach
all 0xb0000 fixture bytes after each run (provider, 32 owners, worker vectors, link pool, merged arrays, reserve allocations)
coverage: worker counts 0..32 including odd, zero and one
capacity below, at, above and zero relative to the total, including null or valid provider pointers
mutation trials: attach/insert services shrink the provider count or swap its array pointer mid-walk (both reread every pass)
limits: Fixture totals reach at most 146 entries (32 workers x 20 slots allowed); the native capacity-doubling loop never terminates when the capacity wraps to 0, and the Python module raises OverflowError there instead (not exercised natively).
Link records are never null: the native key read of a null entry would fault at address 0x10, the Python helper mirrors the read.
The sort is supplied (a reversal stands in); sort stability and algorithm are not asserted.
No live validation or concurrency guarantee.
